body.estimand_functional: \(R_n(c^\dagger)=n^{-1}-C_A(5/8)^{2/3}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\), and for every fixed \(L<U\), \(R_{n,[L,U]}(c^\dagger)=(U-L)^2\{n^{-1}-C_A(5/8)^{2/3}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\}\); the independent allocation \(q^\dagger\) attains the same binary and bounded second-order values, while the terminating exact finite-data evaluator is asserted only for the binary game.

sampling_model.design: The causal game permits every outcome-independent assignment law, including arbitrary dependence across labeled units and zero allocation to an arm. At \(c^\dagger\), the proved all-count converse matches the total procedure under independent \(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\). The bounded-support corollary preserves the chosen design-law class exactly.
sampling_model.units: The kernel is a fixed finite population of \(n\) labeled units with three binary potential outcomes and all eight response types. For outcomes in a fixed interval \([L,U]\), the causal contrast and minimax risk are transferred from the binary game by the exact latent-Bernoulli reduction; no superpopulation sampling is introduced.
sampling_model.treatment: Exactly one of three arm labels is assigned to each unit, and the observation is the assigned label together with its binary outcome.
sampling_model.overlap: No overlap condition is imposed. The common-shift tangent supplies a target-changing direction invisible on every proper allocation face, and the proved local, exterior, and zero-face inequalities make the all-design lower expansion uniform over every allocation count.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no superpopulation nuisance estimation. The lower-prior coordinates are a longitudinal target coordinate, a transverse contrast-orthogonal coordinate, and an independent common shift. Their product score has exact directional information \(J_x(k)+10\{\beta^2+\gamma^2\}/\varepsilon^2\); the fixed-parameter diagonal waits until its threshold absorbs this transverse cost.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2.2 gives the unrestricted two-arm binary game, Theorem 2.3 gives exact bounded-endpoint scaling, and Theorem 3.1 gives \(\rho_n^\star=n^{-1}-C_An^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\).
Theorem 1 optimizes over every two-arm assignment mechanism and measurable estimator and gives the equivalent exact bounded-endpoint game.
Under permutation-invariant law classes and linear estimation schemes, complete randomization with Neyman allocation is minimax.
A first-order local asymptotic minimax bound applies across broad sequential experimental designs, including multiple treatments.
Pairwise-independent inclusion attains the sharp bounded-total minimax risk within the class of unbiased estimators.
Limits of experiments yield asymptotically optimal treatment rules under average and minimax risk criteria in smooth models.
Second-order minimax optimality can be characterized through positive solutions of a problem-specific Schrodinger equation.

body.tldr: For the fixed unequal contrast \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), the unrestricted binary three-arm minimax risk is now proved to satisfy \(R_n(c^\dagger)=n^{-1}-C_A(5/8)^{2/3}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\), and the independent allocation \(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\) attains the same second-order value. The face-robust all-count argument supplies the matching all-procedure lower bound, while the binary evaluator returns terminating finite risk brackets and a total procedure. An exact finite-sample Rao--Blackwell reduction further gives \(R_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathfrak D}(c)=(U-L)^2R_{n,\{0,1\}}^{\mathfrak D}(c)\) for every fixed bounded interval and every fixed class of outcome-independent designs. The remaining sharpness limitation is unrestricted design optimality for general contrasts \(c\), not the fixed contrast \(c^\dagger\).

project_justification.gap: Published exact unrestricted results cover the binary-treatment action space. Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen optimize jointly over all binary-treatment assignment laws and estimators, and Hull gives the equivalent all-mechanism bounded two-arm game; neither treats a three-arm action space. The accepted parent established only the first-order value and the order of the second-order gain. The present result closes the sharp coefficient at the fixed unequal three-arm contrast \(c^\dagger\), while the same unrestricted conclusion for a general permitted contrast remains open.
project_justification.niche: At \(c^\dagger\), the exact eight-response-type geometry and the three-coordinate face-robust prior cover local allocations, positive-count exterior allocations, and every zero-count face without an overlap assumption. This yields an unrestricted three-arm coefficient \(C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\), proves that \(q^\dagger\) has no second-order loss there, and separates that result from the strictly weaker two-arm nature restriction with coefficient \(C_A\).
project_justification.fill: The contribution combines a total independent Airy-feedback procedure, an exact-target generalized van Trees lower ledger uniform over all allocation counts, a computable nonincreasing finite-to-limit tail, and a terminating binary finite-data evaluator. The bounded-endpoint reduction is exact for each finite \(n\): endpoint inclusion proves one direction, and latent Bernoulli completion followed by conditional Jensen proves the other without changing the design class or estimator quantifiers. It transfers both the unrestricted \(c^\dagger\) theorem and the fixed-independent general-contrast theorem to every fixed interval \([L,U]\).

body.related_work: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026), Theorem 2.2, optimize over every assignment mechanism and estimator in the binary-treatment finite-population game; Theorem 2.3 proves exact bounded-endpoint scaling, and Theorem 3.1 proves \(\rho_n^\star=n^{-1}-C_An^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\). Hull (2026), version 3, Theorem 1, likewise optimizes over every assignment mechanism and measurable estimator and gives the equivalent exact bounded two-arm game. Neither paper covers a three-arm action space. Restricting the present nature class to \(Y_i(2)=Y_i(3)\) gives the valid comparison \(R_n(c^\dagger)\ge\rho_n^\star=n^{-1}-C_An^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\), but \(C_A>C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\), so that imported converse is strictly weaker than the proved three-arm coefficient. Bai (2023), Armstrong (2022), and Aronow and Lopatto (2026) impose different model, asymptotic, or estimator restrictions. Hirano and Porter (2009) and Levit (1986) provide limiting-decision and spectral context. Hammer et al. (1996) is only motivation for a prospective complete fixed-horizon binary-endpoint regimen trial; no censored ACTG175 outcome is reanalyzed.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Unrestricted sharpness is proved only for the fixed rational contrast \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\). For every permitted fixed real contrast, the fixed-independent expansion and its exact bounded-endpoint lift are proved, but equality with the unrestricted design game is not claimed. The terminating same-input evaluator remains a binary, fixed-rational-contrast certificate; the analytic bounded-endpoint reduction does not by itself provide a rational encoding for arbitrary real endpoints or contrasts. No growing-\(K\), uniform vanishing-weight, or arbitrary-real computability statement is made. The finite \(K=3,n=3\) label gap remains diagnostic rather than an asymptotic argument.
body.honest_scope: The paper proves the unrestricted sharp binary expansion and equality of the independent second-order value at \(c^\dagger\), together with a terminating binary finite-to-limit certificate. It also proves the exact bounded-endpoint scaling for every fixed interval and every fixed outcome-independent design-law class, so both the unrestricted \(c^\dagger\) result and the general-contrast fixed-independent result have bounded-outcome corollaries. The exact eight-type kernel and effective evaluator remain explicitly binary. Unrestricted sharpness for contrasts other than \(c^\dagger\), growing numbers of arms, uniform vanishing weights, and computation from an unrepresented arbitrary real contrast are outside the claim.
body.interpretation: For a prospective three-regimen trial with the fixed contrast \(c^\dagger\), a trialist may prespecify independent allocation \(q^\dagger\) and the total Airy-feedback procedure knowing that no outcome-independent dependent design and no possibly biased labeled-data estimator improves its second-order minimax coefficient. The binary evaluator supplies finite risk brackets and an all-future error certificate. If all potential outcomes instead lie in a fixed interval \([L,U]\), the explicit latent-Bernoulli conditional-expectation lift is a total procedure and multiplies the corresponding binary minimax risk by \((U-L)^2\). This is a prospective design result, not a reanalysis of censored ACTG175 data.
